issues.detail: Hebrew 'וְהַזּוּרֶה' means 'and the one who crushes/smashes' (from זוּר, to crush), not 'the one who tramples' (which would be רָמַס or דָּרַךְ). The Chinese '踐踏者' (trampler) changes the action from crushing to trampling.

Hebrew 'תִּבָּקַע אֶפְעֶה' means 'a viper will hatch/break forth' (i.e., the crushed egg yields a viper), not 'the viper will be crushed' (which would be passive of בקע with the viper as object). The Chinese '毒蛇必被壓碎' reverses the subject/object: in Hebrew the viper is the subject that emerges, not the object that is crushed.
